name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a scenic hill town at about 1,444 m elevation known for its Angami Naga culture, War Cemetery, and as the base for Hornbill Festival and surrounding highland attractions.
facts: Gateway to Dzukou Valley and Kisama
Host base for annual Hornbill Festival

name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring distinctive mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and carved monoliths dating to the 10th–13th centuries. ASI-protected site with intricate motifs; remnants of the ancient fortified capital.
facts: Mushroom-domed pillars up to 15 ft high
Ancient capital of Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Located near Naga Shopping Arcade / Circuit House

name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland on the banks of the Dhansiri River. Main air and rail entry point; historic Kachari area with multi-ethnic markets and base for highland circuits.
facts: Largest city and main gateway of Nagaland

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum in Dimapur with galleries, science park and Taramandal planetarium. Educational family attraction promoting scientific awareness.
facts: Located at Super Market Lane, Half Nagarjan

name: Green Park
description: Recreational park at 4th Mile inside the State Horticulture Nursery, Dimapur. Greenery, boating, picnic areas and adventure activities for families.

name: Dimapur Jain Temple
description: Historic Digambara Jain temple to Lord Mahavira established in 1947. Important spiritual landmark with intricate glasswork for the local Jain community.
facts: Managed by SD Jain Samaj Dimapur
Additional shrines to Adinath and Bahubali

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and North East Heritage Museum
description: Cultural complex near Dimapur Airport with stone sculpture garden, traditional morungs and museum of northeastern crafts and artefacts.
facts: Near airport, ~3 km from railway station

name: Dhansiri River (Dimapur Section)
description: River flowing along Dimapur giving the city its historic name. Scenic banks for walks and local recreation in the plains.

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling commercial market in central Dimapur selling imported goods, clothing, electronics and local products. Vibrant trading hub.

name: Dimapur City Tower (Clock Tower)
description: Landmark clock tower on Circular Road in central Dimapur. Popular photo spot, often lit during festivals.

name: Longwa Village (Lungwa)
description: Unique Konyak Naga village in Mon district straddling the India-Myanmar international border. The Angh (chief)'s longhouse is famously divided by the border, with parts in each country; villagers hold dual citizenship under the Free Movement Regime. Known for traditional architecture, wood carvings, and headhunting history.
facts: One of the largest villages in Mon district
Official tourist place listed by mon.nic.in

name: Shangnyu Village
description: Prominent Konyak village near Mon featuring a 500-year-old Angh's palace and a large wooden monument/carving believed to be ancient. Declared an ethnic village; rich in traditional sculptures, memorial stones, and Konyak craftsmanship.
facts: Famous for wooden monument and carvings

name: Chui Village
description: Accessible traditional Konyak village near Mon town, known for its grand Angh's house, wooden totems, skull exhibits from the past, and authentic tribal architecture. Serves as an introduction to Konyak culture.
facts: Grand Angh's mansion with traditional totems
Famous for wood carvings and cultural heritage
Easy access for visitors from Mon

name: Mon
description: District headquarters of Mon and gateway to the Konyak heartland. Scenic hill town at about 655-900 m elevation, base for exploring surrounding villages, Veda Peak, and Aoleang Festival; known as the Land of the Anghs.
facts: Home of the Konyak Naga tribe
Base for Longwa, Shangnyu and Veda Peak circuits

name: Veda Peak (Pak Koi)
description: Highest peak in Mon district, about 70 km from the headquarters. Offers panoramic views of the Brahmaputra and Chindwin rivers on clear days, with a nearby waterfall; popular for trekking amid Konyak countryside. Historically associated with early British camps.
facts: Views of Brahmaputra and Chindwin rivers

name: Singphan Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Wildlife sanctuary covering about 23.57 km² in Mon district along the Assam border. Notified in 2009 and declared Singphan Elephant Reserve in 2018 (India's 30th); important elephant corridor with tropical forests, supporting elephants, birds and other fauna.

name: Chenloisho Village
description: One of the larger villages in the Chen area of Mon district near the India-Myanmar border. Features a small museum of traditional Konyak ornaments and artefacts; known for cultural displays and remote highland setting.
facts: Near India-Myanmar border in Chen area
One of the biggest villages in Chen region
Part of official cultural village listings
